name: Bø 1999
question: How do supervised pelvic floor muscle training, vaginal electrical stimulation, and weighted vaginal cones compare with no active treatment for women with genuine stress incontinence?

design.population: Women with clinically and urodynamically confirmed genuine stress urinary incontinence from five centers in southeast Norway.
design.description: Multicenter, assessor-blinded, four-arm randomized superiority trial

verdictNote: Supervised training had the largest standardized pad-test reduction; global four-group P = 0.038.
takeaway: Among 107 analyzed women in a 122-woman trial of genuine stress incontinence, supervised pelvic floor muscle training produced the largest six-month reduction in standardized pad-test leakage (global P = 0.038), exceeding vaginal electrical stimulation by 22.8 g (95% CI 3.8 to 41.8; P = 0.02).

reports.label: Six-month primary report
reports.citation: Bø K, Talseth T, Holme I. "Single blind, randomised controlled trial of pelvic floor exercises, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and no treatment in management of genuine stress incontinence in women." *BMJ.* 1999;318(7182):487-493. doi:10.1136/bmj.318.7182.487

results.measure: Mean change in leakage, baseline to six months (g); global four-group comparison
results.note: PFMT versus stimulation difference in reduction; global four-group P = 0.038. Negative arm changes mean less leakage. Treated-participant analysis (25, 25, 27, and 30 women, respectively).
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, Changes after treatment, p 490

results.measure: Condition rated unproblematic at six months
results.note: P value compares change from baseline in the exercise group with the other groups; five-category self-rating.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Main outcome measures, p 489; Results, Subjective cure, p 491; Discussion, p 492

results.measure: Standardized pad-test leakage <2 g at six months
results.locator: Full text, Results, Objective cure, p 491

results.measure: Women wanting treatment beyond their assigned strategy after six months
results.note: Question asked at the end of assigned treatment.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph after Table 4, p 491

results.measure: Mean change in 24-hour home pad-test leakage, baseline to six months (g); global four-group comparison
results.note: Home test performed on a typical activity day; treated-participant analysis (25, 25, 27, and 30 women, respectively).
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Secondary outcome measures, p 489; Table 2, p 490

results.measure: Mean vaginal squeeze pressure before versus after six months (cm H2O)
results.note: PFMT change exceeded changes with stimulation and cones (P = 0.03); only PFMT improved significantly versus control (P < 0.01).

delivery.label: Assigned treatment protocols
delivery.value: PFMT: 8–12 near-maximal contractions three times daily, held 6–8 seconds with three or four fast contractions added, plus a weekly 45-minute therapist-led class; electrical stimulation: MS 106 Twin intermittent vaginal stimulation at 50 Hz, 0.2 ms pulse width, 0–120 mA and individualized duty cycle for 30 minutes daily; cones: Mabella 20, 40, and 70 g weights for 20 minutes daily; control: continence guard offered.

delivery.label: Pad-test protocol
delivery.value: After catheter emptying, bladder filled with 200 mL saline; 30 seconds running in place and 30 seconds jumping jacks; pad weight change measured.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Main outcome measures, Pad test with standardised bladder volume, p 489

delivery.label: Statistical plan
delivery.value: Kruskal-Wallis global tests for interval-scaled variables and Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel or chi-square tests for categorical variables, with P <0.05 as the significance threshold; primary treated-participant analysis and intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis carrying baseline values forward for missing measurements.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Statistical methods, p 489

delivery.label: Trial flow and treatment adherence
delivery.value: 122 randomized (PFMT 29; stimulation 32; cones 29; control 32); 107 in treated-participant efficacy analysis (25; 25; 27; 30). Mean adherence: PFMT 93% (SE 1.5%); stimulation 75% (SE 2.8%); cones 78% (SE 4.4%).
delivery.locator: Full text, Figure 1, p 489; Results, opening paragraph and Compliance with treatment, pp 489–490

delivery.label: Continence guard use in untreated controls
delivery.value: 14/30 analyzed controls used the offered continence guard; four felt completely dry while wearing it and five felt somewhat better.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph after Table 4, p 491
